description: Use this when you need the custom domains on the signed-in account, including DNS status. Read-only; requires auth; no inputs. Returns {object:"list", data:[{id, domain, status, status_detail, mail, records, warnings, dns}]}. Each record has status valid, missing, or invalid, found from the last check, and hint (null, or {code, message, found_at} saying what to change). warnings is an empty array when none. existing_mail_provider means this hostname already has MX at another provider. Inboxes on your own domain are included on Starter (15 custom domains) and Pro (200 custom domains). Free includes 0 custom domains and returns HTTP 402 plan_limit_exceeded. When the hostname is already an active zone on the operator Cloudflare account, Cooper writes the DNS records and dns.mode is automatic. Cooper does not register a domain or create a zone. A zone that is on that account but not active stays manual. Publish the routing MX hosts, TXT SPF v=spf1 include:_spf.mx.cloudflare.net ~all, the routing DKIM TXT, the cf-bounce MX, SPF, and DKIM records, a DMARC TXT (an existing DMARC record is left as it is), and the _cooper-verify TXT, or point the nameservers at the ones in the response. mail.receiving stays false until the receiving records check out and the catch-all is live. Receiving goes live within a few minutes. status_detail says so while you wait. POST /api/v1/inboxes with domain then creates username@domain. When the hostname is not a zone on the operator account, dns.mode is external. Cooper does not move nameservers. Each record has host, type, value, priority for MX, and ttl. Publish the receiving MX, the return-path MX and one SPF TXT with a single include, the DKIM TXT, and the _cooper-verify TXT at your own DNS host. An existing SPF is merged into that one record. An apex v=spf1 -all does not reject mail whose envelope-from is the return-path host. Do not add a second SPF TXT. A DMARC p=reject record is left as published and blocks mail until DKIM for that domain verifies. Cooper checks the records with public DNS. mail.receiving becomes true after the receiving MX verifies and RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set. mail.sending becomes true after the return-path and DKIM records verify. The receiving MX hostname and the DKIM value come from Resend on that response. Do not invent them. DELETE /api/v1/domains/:id puts back the catch-all that was there before, deletes only the DNS records Cooper created, turns Email Routing off only if Cooper turned it on, and removes the sending domain only if Cooper created it. A Resend domain Cooper created is removed the same way. A cleanup that does not finish keeps the row with status cleanup_failed and deleted false so a later delete can finish it. Failure codes: unauthorized.
name: cooper_list_domains
title: List custom domains
